chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Follow-ups on Chicago: Lil Armstrong, Club Deluxe, Ray Nance and the Swingland
summary: Clarifies the one-night Lil Armstrong job, Joe Hughes' Club De Luxe, and where he heard Ray Nance.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You mentioned that your first job in Chicago was with Lil Armstrong. How long did you work with him?
Just, that one night. A one-night gig.
And you said that you worked for John Litman. Did you work at the Club Deluxe or did you --
Joe Hughes' Club Deluxe. It's across the street from White's Amusement Park.
And so you said that's the first place you said you saw Ray Nance. So Ray Nance was in the floor show?
No that wasn't the first place I saw Ray Nance.
Oh, where was the first place?
Ray Nance was working with Earl Hines.
Before he worked at the Club Deluxe, is that right?

Yeah, I heard Ray Nance when Earl Hines came out here to Los Angeles before I ever left here. He and Trummy Young was with the Band. And they were featured instrumentalist and singers with the band at that time.
So the next time after that that you saw Ray Nance was when you were working at the Club Deluxe?

No, he was still with Earl Hines when I went to Chicago and then he left Earl and I think he worked with Horace Henderson's band for a while. And there was another obscure band, a saxophone player, I think his name was Delbert White. He had a band, all of the bands around other than Earl

It was on Michigan Boulevard, Garfield Boulevard and just off of South Park, west of South Park. Right at almost, between the and South Park. And it took on various names down through the years but it was originally the Swingland.
